title: Did your prompt tweak break your AI? promptfoo catches it
description:
promptfoo is an open-source LLM evaluation and red-teaming tool: an exam for your AI app. Write test cases once, run them against every prompt and model, and see what passed or failed before your customers do.

In this video:
- What promptfoo is and how LLM evals work
- 3 real uses: compare models side by side, red team your app for jailbreaks and prompt injection, run the tests in CI/CD
- The catch: API costs, cloud-generated attacks, free-version limits, and the OpenAI ownership
- Who it's for, an alternative, and how to try it

Three real uses:
1. Compare models: run the same tests on GPT, Claude, Gemini or a local model and see the answers side by side, marked pass or fail
2. Red teaming: generate hundreds of adversarial inputs (jailbreaks, prompt injection and 50+ vulnerability types) and get a report with severity and suggested mitigations
3. CI/CD: run the evals on every change and fail the build when a test fails (promptfoo eval --fail-on-error)

The catch: every test calls a real model, so big test suites mean a real API bill. Red-team attacks are generated by promptfoo's remote service by default; PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_REDTEAM_REMOTE_GENERATION=true turns it off, though the docs say attack quality may drop. The free Community version limits red teaming, remediations, result sharing and API access; team management and RBAC are Enterprise features. Usage telemetry is on by default (PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 turns it off). promptfoo is now part of OpenAI; the team says it remains open source and MIT licensed.

Try it:
npm install -g promptfoo
promptfoo init --example getting-started
cd getting-started
export OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key
promptfoo eval
promptfoo view
(Needs Node.js 22.22 or newer. Also available via brew install promptfoo, pip install promptfoo, or npx promptfoo@latest.)
